content: The brand was originally established in Cuba in 1932. However, the Cuban version of the brand is now exclusively available as a fully machine-made product, limited to only two vitolas. The non-Cuban version of the Troya brand was introduced to the U.S. market in 1985. The original medium-bodied blend was discontinued in 2003 and replaced in 2004 with a milder blend. Additionally, in 2004, the brand expanded its offerings with the introduction of a full-bodied cigar called the Troya X-Tra. In early 2007, the Troya Clasico was launched, a cigar blended and manufactured by Don Pepin Garcia at Tabacalera Cubana in Estelí, Nicaragua. Don Pepin had previously contributed to the development of blends for the other Troya lines, which were the result of collaborative efforts by several individuals. The Troya line is currently manufactured in the Dominican Republic. This line is available in two ranges: one featuring a Cameroon wrapper and the other a Connecticut wrapper. The Cameroon-wrapped cigars are medium-bodied, while the Connecticut-wrapped cigars are mild to medium-bodied. Both ranges use Dominican Piloto Cubano and Olor tobaccos for the filler and binder. These cigars are packaged in boxes containing 24 units. The Troya X-Tra line, which was formerly produced in Estelí, Nicaragua, is now manufactured in the Dominican Republic at the same factory as the main Troya line. Despite its current production location, the X-Tra remains a Nicaraguan puro. It is a medium to full-bodied cigar, with Criollo leaves as the filler and Corojo 99 from the Jalapa Valley of Nicaragua used for both the binder and wrapper. These cigars are also presented in boxes of 24. The Troya Clasico line was introduced to the U.S. market in January 2007 as a limited-edition release. This cigar was blended by Don Pepin Garcia and is manufactured at Tabacalera Cubana in Estelí, Nicaragua. The Clasico is a full-bodied Nicaraguan puro, utilizing tobaccos grown in the Jalapa region of Nicaragua. It features a Corojo Oscuro wrapper, which encases a binder and filler composed of Corojo and Criollo tobaccos. These cigars are offered in boxes containing 20 units.
